newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech prepared for wireless competition.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech prepared for wireless competition.

text.p: Ameritech Corp is prepared to face new competition in its cellular phone markets brought on by the launch of a long-awaited wireless phone network in various U.S. cities.
"This is not something we're going to sit and lose any sleep over," John Rooney, president of Ameritech's cellular and paging group, said in an interview Tuesday.

Earlier, PrimeCo, a venture owned by AirTouch Communications Inc and three regional Bell operating companies, launched Personal Communications Services (PCS) in 16 cities, including Ameritech's Chicago and Milwaukee markets.
"They're going to have to struggle to measure up to what we're spending and doing for our customers already," he said.

Rooney said Ameritech's churn rate -- the percent of subscribers lost -- has been under 12 percent annually for the past three years. He said the rate is considered low in the industry and is the result of superior customer service. Ameritech reported it had 2.3 million cellular subscribers in the third quarter.
"If they come in with the pricing I've seen so far, they're going to be competing with us in the area we like to compete," which is customer service, Rooney said.
And if a pricing war does break out, Ameritech will fight back.
"We will be very competitive in the marketplace," Rooney said. "No one will be taking customers away from us because of any single element."

Ameritech plans to launch its own PCS network in the Cleveland and Indianapolis areas in late 1997, Rooney said, which will use a digital enhanced CDMA (code division multiple access) technology similar to PrimeCo's network. Its Chicago, Milwaukee and other markets use analog networks, which Rooney said at least match PrimeCo's call quality.
"These guys have nothing that I would consider any different," Rooney said.
PrimeCo is a consortium of AirTouch, Bell Atlantic Corp, NYNEX Corp and US West Inc.
